guide:
You check whether retrieved text states the facts of gold evidence sentences.

Use only the retrieved items. Do not use outside knowledge and do not reason
your way to a fact the text does not state; plain rewording, synonyms,
abbreviations and different formatting are fine.

For every fact give one status:
- stated: some item says it, with every specific matching (names, numbers,
  dates, places, who did what, qualifiers).
- contradicted: some item gives a different value for the same specific, such
  as another year or another person.
- missing: neither of the above.
If one item states the fact and another contradicts it, the status is contradicted.

Evidence for stated or contradicted facts: copy one continuous passage from
one item, character for character, with no ellipses or edits, and give that
item's number. Never join separate words into a quote that does not appear as
written; if the words are apart, quote the longer continuous passage that
contains them. A fact spread across items may take several quotes. The quotes
together must contain the words that state every specific of the fact (who,
what, numbers, dates, reasons); a quote that only sets the topic, or stops
before the specific, is not evidence. Missing facts take no evidence. Every quote is checked against the item text by a
program, and a quote that does not appear there counts as missing.

Write the verdict file named in your task as a JSON array with one object per
item, in any order:
{"id": "<item id>", "facts": [{"fact": "S.F", "status": "stated", "evidence": [{"item": 3, "quote": "..."}]}, ...]}
where "S.F" is the fact's label as given (sentence number, fact number).
Give exactly one entry for every fact label of the item. Use only ids from
this file and do not skip any item.

Considering Swift is known for being an Eagles fan – she’s originally from Pennsylvania and even references the team in Gold Rush – her outward support for the Kelce’s team seemed extra telling. Swifties were immediately on high alert, with some capturing Swift and Kelce leaving the stadium together. If that wasn’t enough, extra observant fans were able to note that Kelce’s blue and white post-game outfit was supposedly labelled the “1989 bedroom painting set”, perhaps an intentional reference to Swift’s 2014 album, which she will be re-releasing in October. Swift’s penchant for Easter eggs must be rubbing off on the tight end player. As if this weren’t enough subtle references already, they were also spotted in a “getaway car” together outside the stadium – potentially a nod towards her 2017 track.

When pop culture and sport collide: A timeline of Taylor Swift’s NFL takeover (The Age, 2023-09-26T05:26:05+00:00)
The first link between Swift and Kelce was established in 2016, when Kelce – who helped bring his team to Super Bowl victory in both 2020 and 2023 – played the classic game “Kiss, Marry, Kill”. Speaking with AfterBuzz TV, Kelce was given the options of Swift, Katy Perry and Ariana Grande. He said he’d ultimately kill Grande, marry Perry and kiss Swift. That was about six years ago, but it has more recently set tongues wagging as fans wondered how long the plan for them to meet has been in the works. Cruel Summer Fast-forward seven years, and things started to heat up. In July, speaking on the podcast he shares with his brother, New Heights, Kelce said he intended to give Swift a friendship bracelet with his number on it during her Eras Tour concert in Kansas City.
